title: Quasi-finite affine decomposition after a surjective base change
statement: Let $h:V\to U$ be a quasi-finite morphism [pqf-def-quasifinite] of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]). There exist an affine scheme $U\prime$, a surjective morphism $a:U\prime\to U$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow V\prime=V\times_U U\prime$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product] which is surjective on underlying points (a thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]), such that the composite $Z\xrightarrow{i}V\prime\to U\prime$ is finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category].

proof.text: Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The affine-open finite-presentation theorem, applied to the whole source and target as affine opens, makes $B$ a finitely presented $A$-algebra. Index the finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras of $A$ by inclusion; their union is $A$, and the union has the ring-colimit universal property since a compatible family of ring maps is defined element by element. The index is a small nonempty directed set: adjoining the union of two finite generating sets gives an upper bound. Apply finite-presentation descent to obtain $B_0$ finitely presented over some $A_0$, with $B\cong A\otimes_{A_0}B_0$. The affine quasi-finiteness descent lemma gives a later stage $A_i\to B_i$ which is quasi-finite. Put $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ and $h_0:V_0\to U_0$. Both schemes are of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and hence Noetherian by the cited theorem. The affine fibre-product formula identifies $h$ with the pullback of $h_0$ along $U\to U_0$. We construct the required cover for $h_0$ in steps 2-6, then pull it back in step 7.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: We partition $U_0$ so that $h_0$ becomes finite on each piece. Explicitly, for each reduced closed subscheme $T\subseteq U_0$, apply the locally-quasi-finite base-change lemma and quasi-compact base change to $V_0\times_{U_0}T\to T$. The locally-quasi-finite plus quasi-compact criterion gives quasi-finiteness; the finite-fibres criterion then gives finite fibres and local finite type. This morphism is between affine schemes, hence quasi-separated (its diagonal is induced by the surjection $C\otimes_D C\to C$), and is locally of finite type as just established. The generic-finiteness theorem therefore supplies a dense open $O\subseteq T$ where it is finite. A closed subscheme of the Noetherian affine $U_0$ is Noetherian: its coordinate ring is a quotient, and every quotient ideal is generated by the images of finitely many generators of its inverse image. Take its reduced structure for $T$; the same argument applies. Partition $O$ by reduced locally closed affine subschemes using the affine-partition lemma. Finiteness persists on these pieces: for a finite module generated by $c_1,\ldots,c_r$, its tensor base change is generated by $1\otimes c_1,\ldots,1\otimes c_r$. Repeat on the reduced closed complement $T\setminus O$. The underlying space of $U_0$ is Noetherian by the affine Noetherian-space lemma, so this strict descending chain of closed complements terminates. Beginning with $T=(U_0)_{\mathrm{red}}$ yields finitely many reduced locally closed affine strata $S_t\to U_0$ covering all its points, and $Y_t=V_0\times_{U_0}S_t\to S_t$ is finite. The empty complement is the terminal case.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: For each finite affine map $Y_t\to S_t$, apply the section-cover lemma. It gives a surjective finite locally free $A_t\to S_t$, a closed immersion $Y_t\times_{S_t}A_t\hookrightarrow W_t$, and finitely many closed sections $s_k:A_t\cong W_{t,k}\subseteq W_t$ covering the underlying space of $W_t$. The scheme $A_t$ is affine and Noetherian: a finite algebra is of finite type (module generators also generate it as an algebra), so finite-type preservation of Noetherianity applies to $A_t\to S_t$. Set $Y_{A_t}=Y_t\times_{S_t}A_t$.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: In $A_t$, let $C_k=s_k^{-1}(Y_{A_t})$ and let $D_{k\ell}$ be the equalizer closed subscheme of the two sections $s_k,s_\ell$. These are closed: $C_k$ is a pullback of the closed immersion of $Y_{A_t}$, and $D_{k\ell}$ is the pullback of the diagonal of the affine $W_t\to A_t$, whose coordinate map is the surjective multiplication map. Form the finitely many Boolean atoms of the underlying closed sets $|C_k|$ and $|D_{k\ell}|$: an atom is an intersection of chosen closed sets with the complements of the others, hence is locally closed. Give each atom its reduced induced structure, and apply the affine-partition lemma to it. Each atom is an open subscheme of a reduced closed subscheme of $A_t$. The latter has a Noetherian coordinate ring, being a quotient of the coordinate ring of $A_t$. Its basic affine opens have Noetherian coordinate rings (localizing finite ideal generators still generates every localized ideal). The atom has a finite cover by such basic opens, since every open in a Noetherian space is quasi-compact. Thus it is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, hence Noetherian, as required by the affine-partition lemma. We obtain a finite partition of $A_t$ by reduced locally closed affine schemes $R$. The ambient section cover remains a cover after this base change: if $W_t=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and the sections have ideals $J_k$, a prime of a base-changed coordinate ring contracts to a prime of $C$ containing some $J_k$, and therefore contains the extended ideal $J_k$. Thus it lies on the corresponding pulled-back section. On each $R$, every $C_k\times_{A_t}R$ and every $D_{k\ell}\times_{A_t}R$ has either all points of $R$ or no points. In the former case it equals $R$ as a scheme: its ideal $J$ in a reduced affine ring has $V(J)=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and the reduced-ideal-intersection lemma applied to $J,J$ gives $J=J\cap J=0$. In the latter case the closed subscheme is empty. Thus each base-changed section is either contained in $Y_R$ as a scheme or disjoint from it, and two sections either coincide as schemes or are disjoint.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: Fix one such $R$. Choose one representative of every equality class of sections that is contained in $Y_R=Y_{A_t}\times_{A_t}R$; let their number be $n_R$, which may be zero. They are pairwise disjoint closed subschemes of $Y_R$, each isomorphic to $R$, and their union contains every point of $Y_R$: the ambient sections cover all points, and a section whose inverse image of $Y_R$ is empty contributes none. Write $R=\operatorname{Spec}D$, $Y_R=\operatorname{Spec}C$, and let $I_1,\ldots,I_{n_R}$ be the ideals of these closed sections, with $C/I_j\cong D$ as $D$-algebras. Disjointness gives pairwise comaximal ideals. The Chinese remainder theorem gives $C/(\bigcap_j I_j)\cong D^{n_R}$. Consequently $E_R=\coprod_{j=1}^{n_R}R\to Y_R$ is a closed immersion by the quotient description, and is surjective on points by the covering just proved; it is a thickening. For $n_R=0$, the covering says $Y_R$ is empty, and the same assertion uses the empty scheme and the zero ring. The morphism $E_R\to R$ is etale by the coproduct-copies theorem and finite because $D^{n_R}$ is a module generated by its finitely many coordinate idempotents. This proves finite etaleness without asserting that the nonreduced $Y_R\to R$ is etale.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: Let $T_0$ be the finite disjoint union of all the schemes $R$ obtained for every $t$, and let $E_0$ be the corresponding disjoint union of their $E_R$. The composite $T_0\to U_0$ is surjective: the $S_t$ partition $U_0$, every $A_t\to S_t$ is surjective, and the $R$ partition $A_t$. A finite disjoint union of affine schemes is affine: for rings $D_b$ the spectrum of $\prod_b D_b$ decomposes into the basic opens of the coordinate idempotents, with the $b$-th localization equal to $D_b$. This includes the empty product, the zero ring. Under the resulting identification $T_0=\coprod R$, the scheme $V_0\times_{U_0}T_0$ restricts on its open-and-closed component $R$ to $Y_R$ by the fibre-product universal property. The maps $E_R\to Y_R$ therefore assemble to a closed immersion $E_0\to V_0\times_{U_0}T_0$, since on each component it is the quotient map already written in step 5; it is surjective on points. Its composite $E_0\to T_0$ is finite etale: the finite affine algebra on each open-and-closed base component is $D_b^{n_b}$, and etaleness there is the identity-coproduct etaleness of step 5. Both assertions are checked on these disjoint affine charts. More explicitly, local finite presentation and flatness are checked at each source point on its component $E_R\to R$, whose local rings and affine neighbourhoods are also those of the assembled map. Its diagonal is the disjoint union of the component diagonals: fibre products between different base components are empty. Each component diagonal is an open immersion, so the assembled diagonal is an open immersion. Thus the etale definition applies (Stacks 02GI, 02GV, 02GE). For finiteness, an affine base open decomposes into its finitely many intersections with the open-and-closed $R$; these intersections are affine, and the inverse image has coordinate algebra the finite product of their finite-copy algebras. The coordinate idempotents generate this algebra as a module over the product base ring, verifying the finite-morphism definition.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: Finally put $U\prime=U\times_{U_0}T_0$ and $Z=U\times_{U_0}E_0$. The affine fibre-product formula makes $U\prime$ affine. Surjectivity of $T_0\to U_0$ persists under base change, so $a:U\prime\to U$ is surjective. Reassociating fibre products by their universal property identifies $V\times_U U\prime$ with the pullback of $V_0\times_{U_0}T_0$ along $U\to U_0$. The closed immersion $E_0\to V_0\times_{U_0}T_0$ stays a closed immersion and stays surjective on points by the two cited base-change lemmas. Thus its pullback $i:Z\hookrightarrow V\times_U U\prime$ is a thickening. Finite etaleness of $E_0\to T_0$ persists under the base-change functor in the finite-etale category, yielding $Z\to U\prime$ finite etale. These are exactly the clauses of the item.
